doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

title: Bassists who helped him: Truck Parham and others
summary: Truck Parham shows him double stops and other bassists give him strings.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Were you taught music in any formal way by music teachers in school or anyplace else?

No. I had some -- there was a bass player named Truck Parham - saw me out on the street, you know, with my fiddle, he said, "Come by the house" -- and I went by his house one day; you know, I didn't have no money to pay him but he wanted to help me -- a young kid, you know -- and he showed me how he played double stops. Then there was another bassist out there, Henry Ford, and Taupus Dean, and a bassist named Walter Williams. I don't know what ever happened to him -- he used to give me strings whenever he'd see me, because I couldn't afford to buy a set, so he would give me some old strings and ....
